issues.title: Initial friction finding the Assessment feature
issues.body: Two teachers mistook the Teaching Aide for the Assessment feature. Both found the right one in the end.

shot.alt: Class dashboard in the study sandbox. The Teaching Aide and Assessments tabs sit side by side, highlighted.

issues.short: Unclear what the AI will create
issues.title: Unclear expectations from the Assessment feature
issues.body: Some teachers expected the AI to write the questions. They typed what they wanted and left the answer key blank.

shot.alt: The Description field in Create Assessment, highlighted, holding a one-line request for an essay.

issues.title: Unsure where to add questions
issues.body: The field for questions is labeled “Description”. Teachers looked elsewhere before they tried it.

shot.alt: The label of the questions field, highlighted. It reads Description.

quote.text: I gotta be honest, that was not clear that the Description is where my assessment questions would be.

issues.short: Pick a rubric or “Create with Claire”?
issues.title: Not sure how to add the rubric
issues.body: Teachers picked the General Rubric from the dropdown, then clicked “Create with Claire” as well.

shot.alt: Rubric dropdown with Rubric | ESSAY selected and the Create with Claire button right below it, highlighted.

issues.title: Unable to understand the “Include in Gradebook” setting
issues.body: Every teacher skipped the toggle. After grading, they couldn’t find the grades in the gradebook.

shot.alt: Grading Details with the Include in Gradebook toggle, highlighted.

issues.short: Can't find how to edit the draft
issues.title: Unsure where to edit the assessment
issues.body: Teachers clicked the assessment row to edit it, and the AI Grader opened. Most never noticed the pencil icon.

shot.alt: Assessments list on the class dashboard. The small pencil icons that open the editor are highlighted.

quote.text: That was not intuitive at all… If I wasn’t being assisted, I would have spent a lot of time clicking around mindlessly trying to find the document I just created

issues.short: Can't find the new rubric to attach
issues.title: Could not find the created rubric
issues.body: The new rubric opened in another tab. Teachers expected it to attach itself and had to go back and select it again.

shot.alt: The rubric dropdown in Create Assessment, highlighted. Teachers had to come back here to select the rubric they had just made.

quote.text: I would think the rubric would attach itself after making it.

issues.title: Did not understand the rating scales
issues.body: Scales such as Bloom’s Taxonomy and Advancement Levels didn’t match the terms their districts use.

shot.alt: Rating Scales dropdown, highlighted: Bloom’s Taxonomy, Advancement Levels, Reaching Standard and Depth of Knowledge.

issues.short: No sign the rubric was saved
issues.title: No system feedback after creating a rubric
issues.body: When the rubric appeared, teachers looked for a sign it was saved. One tried to save it as a PDF.

shot.alt: Top of the AI-generated rubric page, highlighted: an editor toolbar with no Save button or confirmation.

issues.title: Confusion between general and specific rubrics
issues.body: Teachers paused between “general” and “specific” rubrics. Few found the hover text that explains them.

shot.alt: Type of Rubric dropdown, highlighted: General Rubrics for Standards and Specific Rubrics for Assessments.

issues.short: AI Grader sits below the teacher's box
issues.title: Trouble finding the AI Grader
issues.body: The teacher’s feedback box sits above the AI Grader. Teachers scrolled down to read the AI, then back up to write.

shot.alt: Grading panel. The teacher’s feedback box comes first; the AI Grader header, highlighted, sits below it.

issues.short: Feedback written for teachers, not students
issues.title: AI feedback needs student-facing language
issues.body: The AI’s feedback was detailed and written in teacher language. Teachers expected to rewrite it for students.

shot.alt: The AI Grader’s overview of a sample essay, highlighted, written in teacher language.

issues.title: Desire to edit AI-generated feedback
issues.body: Teachers double-clicked the AI feedback to edit it like a document. Nothing happened.

shot.alt: The AI Grader’s extended report table, highlighted. It can’t be edited.

issues.short: No Save, no sign grades were sent
issues.title: Saving grade and feedback
issues.body: Grades save without any sign of it. Teachers searched for a Save button and worried students would never see their work.

shot.alt: Final grade field and the Return Grade button, highlighted. There is no Save button.

quote.text: I would feel a lot more reassured if I could click Save somewhere.
